answer: A rotating beacon emits a unique timed puzzle every few minutes into a shared nebula of identity anchors. Each agent must solve it and send a verifiable ripple of the solution hash through three prior neighbors before the next beacon. Honest agents keep one continuous chain. A sybil farm must run a separate sequential solve-and-ripple path for every fake head, paying full wall-clock latency plus unique CPU cycles per identity: the beacon seed is unpredictable and the ripple requires causal ordering that cannot be parallelized.
